caution: You are not obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so, but whatever you say will be taken down in writing and may be given in evidence.

start.h: Start — when, where and why you were there
l: On [day] [date] I was on duty in [uniform / plain clothes] from [station], on [foot patrol / mobile patrol in (call sign, vehicle reg)], with [members present — names and registered numbers].

At [time] I [received a call from (Control / the caller) — PULSE incident (ref) — reporting (what was reported, in the words used) / saw (what first drew my attention) / was asked by (who) to (what)].
I arrived at [exact location — street, number or landmark, which side, inside or outside] at [time].
Conditions: [daylight / dusk / dark]; lighting [street lights working / poor / none]; weather [dry / rain / wind]; [how busy it was — people and traffic present].
start.why: Everything that follows is judged against what you knew, and when. The time you arrived and what you were told before you got there frame the rest of the entry.

l: [Person 1]: [name, date of birth and address if known — and how I know them: ID produced / given verbally / PULSE check / known to me]. If not known: [sex, approx. age, height, build, hair, clothing top to bottom, distinguishing marks].
Role: [suspect / injured party / witness / caller / bystander]. Their condition when I arrived: [what I saw — standing, on the ground, injured, distressed, calm].
[Person 2, 3 …]: as above.
Anyone who left before I could speak to them: [description, direction of travel, time, on foot / vehicle (reg)].
people.why: Descriptions written at the time are what identification evidence is tested against later.

l: [Name / description] told me at [time], in words to the effect of: “[as close to word for word as possible]”.
I wrote this down [at the time / at (time)] and [read it back to them / did not read it back because (reason)].
Anyone who saw it: [name, contact details, where they were standing, what they could see from there, for how long].
Anyone who declined to give details: [description, what they said, time].
account.why: Write what was said, not your summary of it. A first account is often the most valuable — and the most closely examined.

words.h: Questions and answers at the scene
l: Once I suspected [the person] of [offence], before any question about it, I cautioned them at [time]: “You are not obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so, but whatever you say will be taken down in writing and may be given in evidence.” Reply: “[word for word]”.
Question: “[exact words]” — Answer: “[exact words]” — at [time]. (One line per question and answer.)
Read over to [the person] at [time]; invited to sign: [signed at (time) / declined — their words: “(…)”].
Anything said without being asked: “[word for word]” at [time] — and what, if anything, prompted it.
words.why: Caution once you suspect the person. Record questions and answers word for word, read them over and offer them for signature. A breach of the Judges’ Rules is weighed by the trial judge.

l: At [time] at [exact place] I arrested [name / description] under [power — Act and section] for [offence].
My grounds, in order: [1. …  2. …  3. …] — see the reasonable-suspicion prompts.
I told them they were under arrest and why, in plain words: “[exact words]”. Reply: “[word for word]”.
Cautioned at [time]. Reply: “[word for word]”.
Handcuffs: [not used / used at (time) because (the specific risk I saw — not routine)]. Other force: [none / what, why, for how long].
Searched on arrest by [member] at [time]: [nothing found / (item) found in (where on the person)] — exhibit [ref].
Conveyed to [station] in [vehicle], arriving at [time]. Handed to the member in charge, [name / registered number], at [time].
arrest.why: Tell the person they’re under arrest and the reason in ordinary language. Handcuff because of a specific risk, not as a routine. The arrival time and the member in charge’s decision start the custody record.

l: Injuries I saw: [what, where on the body, size, bleeding / swelling / marks] on [whom], at [time].
Photographed by [who] at [time] — [number] photos. Their account of how it happened: “[word for word]”.
Medical attention: [offered at (time) — reply “(…)” / ambulance called at (time), arrived (time) / taken to (hospital) / refused — their words].
Any injury to me or another member: [what, how, first aid, photographed].
injuries.why: Harm (s.3) and serious harm (s.4) are proved by what was seen and recorded early, then by the medical evidence.

l: Exhibit [ref — e.g. your initials and number]: [item], found [exactly where] by [who] at [time]. Packaged in [bag / seal no.] at [time]; handed to [who] at [time]. Every hand it passed through: [ ].

CCTV: cameras seen at [locations — business names, poles, buses, doorbells]. Owner or operator: [name, contact]. Asked to preserve at [time]; overwrite period [ ]; viewed or collected by [who] at [time].
Photos or video taken by me: [what, when, on which device].
Forensic opportunities: [fingerprints / DNA / footwear marks — where]; scene preserved by [who] from [time] to [time].
evidence.why: Continuity is proved hand by hand. Gardaí must look for CCTV and keep what may help either side — evidence offered and not collected has lost cases.

l: Body-worn camera: [switched on at (time) / not issued / not switched on because (reason)]. I told [the person] they were being recorded: [yes, at (time) / no — why].
Patrol car camera, phone or other recordings: [what, by whom]. Footage [uploaded / retained / flagged] by [who] at [time].
bwc.why: If you say it was recorded, the footage will be asked for. If it wasn’t, say why.

l: Outcome: [arrested / charged / summons to follow / fixed charge notice / adult caution / referred to the Juvenile Liaison Officer / advice given / no offence disclosed].
I left at [time]. PULSE incident [ref], created at [time] by [ ]. Sergeant [name / registered number] told at [time].
Still to do: [statements, CCTV, enquiries — and by when].
This entry was written at [time] on [date], at [place]. [If not made at the time: why, and where my first note was made.]
end.why: When you wrote it matters as much as what you wrote. If the entry was made later, say so and say why.

l: Power: [Act and section]. My grounds before the search, in order: [1. …  2. …  3. …].
I told [the person] who I am and that I was searching them under [power] because [reason], in plain words: “[exact words]”. Reply: “[word for word]”.
Searched by [name, sex] at [where — how private] — [which parts of the body / clothing / bag], from [time] to [time]. Present: [ ].
Found: [item], [exactly where on the person or in the bag], at [time] — exhibit [ref]. Or: nothing found.
Force used: [none / what and why]. Complaint, injury or distress: [none / what, and what I did].
search.why: The person must be told, in plain words, the power and the reason. The grounds must be yours and specific to this person — not the area, not their record.

l: Their exact words, including any abuse, with times: “[ ]” at [time]; “[ ]” at [time].
What they did, described rather than labelled: [e.g. stepped to within (distance) of my face, pointed, clenched fists, walked away and came back] at [time].
Signs about their state, described not diagnosed: [smell of alcohol, slurred speech, unsteady, confused about time or place, distressed — and their words].
What I did to calm things, in my words: “[ ]” at [time]. Options I offered: [ ].
Any threat to complain or allegation, word for word: “[ ]” at [time]. My reply: “[ ]”.
Who saw or recorded it: [members, independent witnesses, CCTV, body-worn camera from (time)].
difficult.why: If a complaint may follow, the entry is your account of the facts. Write what was said and done, at the time — not how you felt about it. Open the complaint-proof entry for the full version.

l: What force or contact: [punch / push / kick / spit / object thrown — which hand, how many times, where on the body] at [time], at [exact spot].
Or the threat of immediate force: what was said or done that made [injured party] believe it was about to happen: [words, gestures, distance between them]. What they believed: “[their words]”.
Consent: [injured party] says they did not consent: “[their words]”. Any suggestion of an agreed fight or horseplay: [ ].
Lawful excuse: anything said about self-defence, defending someone else or property: “[word for word]”.
State of mind (intent or recklessness): what the suspect said or did before and after: [ ].
sec.why: Each point to prove needs a fact behind it: the force or the threat, no consent, no lawful excuse, and the state of mind.

l: What force: [punch / kick / weapon or object — which, how many times, where on the body] at [time], at [exact spot].
Consent and lawful excuse: [injured party’s words]; anything the suspect said about self-defence: “[word for word]”.
The harm: [injury to body or mind — pain, swelling, cuts, bruising, unconsciousness] — what I saw at [time], and what [injured party] described: “[ ]”.
Medical evidence to obtain: [hospital / GP / report — who, by when].
Weapon or object: [what, where now] — exhibit [ref].
sec.why: Harm includes pain and injury to the mind. Intent or recklessness goes to the assault, not to the harm — so record the act and the injury separately.

l: What was done: [force, weapon, number of blows, where on the body] at [time], at [exact spot] — seen by [ ].

Serious harm: [injury creating a substantial risk of death / serious disfigurement / substantial loss or impairment of mobility or of a body part or organ] — what I saw, and what medical staff said ([name, role], at [time]).
Weapon: [what, where found, by whom] — exhibit [ref]. Scene preserved from [time] by [who]; cordon at [ ].
Suspect’s words before, during and after: “[word for word]”.
sec.why: Record the injuries exactly as seen; the medical evidence will grade them later. Preserve the scene and the weapon early.

entries.t: Threats to kill or cause serious harm — s.5 NFOAP 1997

l: The threat, word for word: “[ ]” — made [in person / by phone / text / social media / letter] at [time] on [date].
To whom: [the recipient / a third person — who].
How the recipient took it: “[their words]” — did they believe it would be carried out, and why: [history, weapon seen, previous violence].
Evidence of the message: [screenshots — by whom, when; phone seen; account names, numbers] — exhibit [ref].
Suspect’s account: “[word for word]”.
sec.why: The offence turns on the words used and the intention that they be believed — capture both exactly.

l: Each act, one per line — [date, time, what happened: following / watching / pestering / besetting / calls / messages / posts], and the evidence for it: [messages, call logs, CCTV, witnesses].
How it was done: [in person / phone / social media — accounts, numbers].
Effect on [injured party], in their words: [serious interference with their peace and privacy / alarm / distress / harm]: “[ ]”.
Any warning or request to stop given before: [by whom, when, words used].
Why a reasonable person would realise the effect: [frequency, content, persistence after being asked to stop].
sec.why: Harassment is a course of conduct. Build the list act by act, with the evidence for each, and the effect in the person’s own words.

l: The property: [description, quantity, serial numbers, value], owner: [name / business].
What the suspect did: [took it / concealed it / left without paying / passed the tills] — seen by [who] at [time]; CCTV [ ].
No consent: [owner / staff member] says: “[word for word]”.
Dishonesty — no claim of right: what the suspect said about why: “[word for word]”.
Intention to deprive: [what they did with it — concealed, sold, discarded, left the premises].
Recovered: [where, condition, returned to (who) at (time) / kept as exhibit (ref)].
sec.why: Each element needs a fact: appropriation, no consent, dishonesty and the intention to deprive. What the suspect said about why often decides dishonesty.

l: The building or part of it: [house / flat / shed / shop store room / staff-only area] at [address or description].
Entry: [point of entry, damage, marks, open door or window] — photographed by [ ] at [time].
Trespass: [owner / occupier] says no permission: “[word for word]”; anything showing the suspect knew they had no right to be there: [ ].
Intent, or what was done inside: [what was taken, damaged or disturbed].
Forensics: [marks, prints, footwear, blood — preserved by (who) until (time)].
Recent possession: anything from the premises found with the suspect — [what, where, when, what they said about it].
sec.why: Part of a building counts, and so does entering with intent. Record exactly which part was entered and how.

l: Property taken: [what, value, owner].
Force or fear: [what force was used / what was said or done to put (the person) in fear of immediate force] — exact words: “[ ]”; weapon [seen / claimed — what].
Timing: the force or threat was [immediately before / at the time of] the stealing, and in order to steal: [what shows that].
Suspect(s): [descriptions], direction of travel, vehicle, time.
Injured party’s condition and words: “[ ]”.
sec.why: Robbery is theft plus force or fear of force, used in order to steal — record the sequence carefully.

entries.t: Making gain / causing loss by deception — s.6 CJ(T&FO)A 2001

l: What was said or done that was false: [exact words, documents, messages, cards used] — when and where.
Who was deceived, and what they did because of it: [handed over money or goods / provided a service / refrained from (…)].
The gain or loss: [amount, how paid — card, transfer, cash], account and card details for later production orders: [ ].
Dishonesty: what the suspect said when asked: “[word for word]”.
Documents and devices: [what, seized from whom] — exhibit [ref].
sec.why: Prove the false representation, that it caused the act, and the gain or loss — then the dishonesty.

l: The property and why I believe it is stolen: [crime report ref, owner identified, serial numbers matched].
How the suspect had it: [received it / kept it / moved it / sold it / helped someone else] — when and where.
Knowledge or recklessness: [price paid against real value, where and when bought, from whom, receipts] and what they said: “[word for word]”.
Otherwise than in the course of stealing: [why they weren’t the thief, if that’s the case].
sec.why: Handling turns on what the person knew or suspected — record the circumstances of the purchase in detail.

l: What was damaged and how: [property, location, extent] — photographed by [ ] at [time].
Owner: [name / business]; no permission: “[their words]”.
How the suspect did it: [seen by whom, CCTV, tool or object used].
Lawful excuse claimed: “[word for word]”.
Intent or recklessness: [what they said or did before and after].
Cost of repair: [quote — who, when].
sec.why: Record the damage before it’s cleaned up or repaired, and the owner’s words on permission.

entries.t: Possession of a controlled drug — s.3 MDA 1977

l: What was found: [description, quantity, packaging], exactly where [pocket, bag, vehicle, room], by [who] at [time].
Control and knowledge: whose [bag / vehicle / room] it was, and what the person said: “[word for word]”.
Field test: [not done / result — an indication only].
Exhibit: sealed in [bag no.] at [time], lodged in [drugs safe / property store] at [time] for analysis.
Any claim of lawful possession (e.g. prescription): [details].
sec.why: Possession means control plus knowledge. Record who controlled the place it was found and what was said about it.
cases: Minister for Posts and Telegraphs v Campbell

entries.t: Possession for sale or supply — s.15 MDA 1977

l: What was found: [description, quantity, packaging], exactly where, by whom, at [time].
Supply indicators: [how it was divided — number and size of deals], [scales], [bags], [tick lists], [cash — amount, denominations, where kept], [phones — numbers, messages seen].
Control and knowledge: “[what the person said]”.
Admissions about supply, word for word: “[ ]”.
Value: [estimate], and who will give value evidence (s.15A threshold €13,000).
sec.why: Intent to supply is proved by circumstances — quantity, packaging, cash, phones and lifestyle. Record each one.

entries.t: Intoxication in a public place — s.4 CJ(PO)A 1994

l: Public place: [street name / description — open to the public].
Signs of intoxication: [speech, smell, balance, eyes, behaviour] and what they said about drink or drugs: “[ ]”.
Why there was a reasonable apprehension of danger to them or others: [traffic, falling, aggression, alone at night, vulnerable].
Fixed charge notice: [offered — FCN no. / not offered — why]. Under 18: [no FCN — Children Act route].
Welfare: [left with (who) / taken (where) / medical attention].
sec.why: The offence needs danger, not just drink. Write down why you apprehended danger.

entries.t: Threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour — s.6 CJ(PO)A 1994

l: Public place: [street name / description — and why it is public].
The words or behaviour, word for word: “[ ]” — gestures [ ], aimed at [whom], how loud, for how long.
Who was present and affected: [members of the public — number, their reaction].
Intent to provoke a breach of the peace, or recklessness: [what made a breach of the peace likely — others reacting, squaring up].
Fixed charge notice: [offered — FCN no. / not offered — why].
sec.why: Record the exact words and the public place. Courts have dismissed charges where the public place wasn’t proved.

entries.t: Failure to comply with a direction — s.8 CJ(PO)A 1994

l: Public place: [street name / description].
What I saw that founded the direction: [the s.4 / s.5 / s.6 / s.9 conduct, or loitering that gave reasonable apprehension for safety, property or the peace] — in detail.
The direction, word for word: “[e.g. I am directing you to stop (…) and to leave (…) immediately in a peaceable and orderly manner]” at [time].
Whether I told them that not complying is an offence: [yes — exact words / no].
Their reply: “[ ]”. What they did instead: [stayed / came back / carried on] — at [time], after [how long].
Arrest at [time]: words used: “[ ]”.
sec.why: Record the conduct that justified the direction and the direction itself, word for word.
cases: DPP v Unnamed youth (s.5 offensive conduct, 2015)

entries.t: Breach of a domestic violence order — s.33 DVA 2018

l: The order: [safety / barring / interim barring / emergency barring / protection], made by [court] on [date], terms: [ ], expires: [ ]. How I confirmed it: [copy seen / PULSE].
Notice: how the respondent knew of it — [served on (date) by (who) / present in court / told by me at (time)].
The breach: [exactly what was done or said — words, acts], [date, time], seen or heard by [who].
Children present: [names / ages, where, what they saw or heard].
Arrest: [s.35 DVA 2018 at (time) — words used / not arrested — why].
sec.why: Prove the order, that the person knew of it, and the breach. Get the order details and the proof of service every time.

l: Relationship: [intimate relationship — current / former, how long].
The pattern, one line per incident: [date — what happened: isolation from family, monitoring, threats, control of money, degrading treatment] — evidence: [messages, bank records, witnesses, diary].
Effect, in their words: [fear of violence on at least two occasions / serious alarm or distress with a substantial effect on day-to-day life]: “[ ]”.
Who else has seen it: [family, friends, neighbours, colleagues — contact details].
sec.why: Coercive control is proved by the pattern and its effect. Build the timeline with the evidence for each incident.

entries.t: Unauthorised taking of a vehicle — s.112 RTA 1961

l: Vehicle: [reg, make, model, colour] — registered owner: [name, how checked].
Use or possession by the suspect: [driving / in the driver’s seat / in control] — seen by [who] at [time].
No consent: owner says: “[word for word]”. Any lawful authority claimed: “[ ]”.
Passengers: [who, and whether they knew it was taken].
Condition of the vehicle: [damage, ignition, keys] — photographed.
sec.why: If there’s intention to deprive the owner permanently, consider theft instead.

l: What I saw, in order: [speed — estimate and how I judged it, road position, manoeuvres, overtaking, signals, distance followed, for how long].
Public place: [road name, speed limit, layout].
Conditions: [traffic actually present and to be expected, pedestrians, weather, lighting, road surface].
Who was put at risk: [vehicles braking or swerving, pedestrians stepping back — who].
Pursuit: [blue lights and siren from (time), route, speeds].
Driver identified by: [ ]. Dashcam and CCTV: [where, preserved by (who) at (time)].
sec.why: Danger is judged on all the circumstances — record the conditions as well as the driving.

l: Item: [€(denomination) note / coin], serial number [ ], [quantity].
Why it appeared counterfeit: [feel of the paper, watermark, hologram, security thread, colour-changing number, UV pen result] — checked by [who] at [time].
Where it was passed: [business, till], to [staff member — name or description], at [time]. Goods or change given: [what, value].
How the suspect says they got it: “[word for word]”.
Anything that shows they knew or believed it was counterfeit: [several notes, matching serial numbers, new notes, buying small items with large notes, discarding notes, what they said].
Other notes found on them or nearby: [number, denominations, serial numbers, where] — exhibits [refs].
Handled by the edges and sealed separately in [bag no.]; sent for examination under current procedure by [who] on [date].
sec.why: Knowledge or belief is usually what’s in dispute. Record every fact that bears on it, and the account they gave. Check the section (Part 5, CJ(T&FO)A 2001) against the revised Act.

entries.t: Drink or drug driving — at the roadside

l: At [time] I [saw (vehicle reg, make, colour) being driven at (place) — (the manner of driving) / stopped it at a checkpoint authorised by (rank, name) for (time) to (time) / attended a collision at (place)].
Driver: [name / description], identified by [licence / other]. Others in the vehicle: [ ].
sec.why: Record why the vehicle was stopped, and who authorised any checkpoint.

l: Signs I observed: [smell of alcohol, speech, eyes, balance, behaviour] and any admission: “[word for word]”.
Did they mention drinking in the last 20 minutes? [no / yes — “(their words)” — so I waited from (time) to (time) before testing].
Roadside breath test: required under [s.9 / s.10 / other — section] at [time], device [ID / serial], result [pass / fail / warn], shown to the driver at [time].
Drug test if done: oral fluid, [device], result [ ] at [time].
sec.why: There’s no general duty to wait 20 minutes before a roadside test or to ask when the last drink was — but wait if you have reason to suspect a very recent drink, and note it.

l: At [time] I formed the opinion that [the driver] had committed an offence under [s.4 / s.5 RTA 2010] because: [everything — the driving, the signs, the admission, the result].
Arrested at [time] under [s.4(8) / s.5 / other], words used: “[ ]”. Cautioned. Reply: “[word for word]”.
Vehicle: [left secured at (place) / removed by (who) under (power) at (time)].
sec.why: The threshold for the opinion is low, but write down everything it rested on. A different offence needs its own opinion.

entries.t: Drink or drug driving — station procedure

l: Arrived at [station] at [time]. Handed to the member in charge, [name / registered number], at [time]. Custody record opened; information on rights given at [time].
sec.why: Who the member in charge was, and when, matters if the procedure is challenged.

l: Observation to make sure nothing was taken by mouth: started at [time] by [name]; ended at [time].
Interrupted? [no / yes — what happened (looked away, machine in use) — restarted at (time) because (reason)].
Operator: [name — trained]. If we waited for a trained operator: requested at [time], arrived at [time].
Requirement under s.12 at [time], words: “[ ]”. Told the consequences of refusing or failing: [yes — words / no].
Specimens at [time] and [time]; reading [µg/100ml].
Two statements printed. Signed by me at [time], then by [the driver] at [time]. One given to them at [time].
sec.why: Only unreasonable delay needs explaining — but note the reason for every wait. The garda signs the statement first; signed in the wrong order, it can’t be relied on.

l: Why: [device unavailable / medical reason — (what)].
Designated doctor or nurse [name] called at [time], arrived at [time]; specimen taken at [time].
Containers sealed and labelled; one offered to the person at [time]: [taken / declined].
sec.why: Record the reason for the change and every time in the chain.

l: Charged / released at [time] by [who]; bail [station / court date].
This entry was written at [time] on [date].
Location: [road, junction, direction of each vehicle, speed limit, layout, markings, lighting, surface, weather].
Vehicles: [reg, make, model, colour, damage — where and how much; final positions — photographed or sketched].
Drivers: [names, licence numbers, insurance — company and policy, owner]. Each driver’s account in their words: “[ ]”.
Injured: [who, injuries, ambulance called at (time), arrived at (time), hospital].
Witnesses: [names, contacts, where they were, what they saw].
Evidence: [skid marks, debris, measurements, dashcam, CCTV, phone use — enquiries to make].
Requirements made: [breath test at (time) — result], [production of documents — where, within how long].
Scene: [traffic management, road closed from (time) to (time), collision investigator called at (time)].
sec.why: A collision scene changes fast. Record positions, marks and accounts before they’re gone.

l: E-scooter: [make, model, colour, serial number], [motor power / top speed if known].
Rider: [name / description, age]; helmet: [ ]; passenger carried: [ ]; phone in use: [ ].
Where and how it was ridden: [road / footpath / cycle lane], [speed, manner].
Collision, if any: [with whom or what], injuries, damage, CCTV.
Whether it meets the legal definition of a powered personal transporter, or is a vehicle that needs tax, insurance and a licence — the facts: [ ] (check the current rules in Tools > E-scooters).
Action: [advice / fixed charge / seizure under (power) / prosecution].
sec.why: Whether it’s a legal e-scooter or an unregistered vehicle decides everything else — record the facts that answer that.

entries.t: SPSV check — taxi, hackney or limousine

l: Vehicle: [reg], [taxi / hackney / limousine], vehicle licence number [ ] — disc displayed: [yes / no]; roof sign: [ ]; meter: [on / off / not fitted].
Driver: [name], SPSV driver licence [number, expiry]; driver display (ID) shown: [yes / no]; photo matches the driver: [yes / no].
Passengers on board: [number]; booking: [hailed / app (which) / phone]; fare charged or agreed: [ ].
Insurance certificate, NCT and roadworthiness: [produced / to be produced at (station) within (days)].
What I required, and under which power: [ ]. Replies: “[word for word]”.
Outcome: [no issue / fixed charge / report to the NTA (ref) / summons].
sec.why: Write licence numbers exactly as displayed — they’re what the NTA and the court will check.

entries.t: Public order incident — fight, crowd or disturbance

l: Number of people involved: [ ]. What each person did, one line each: [description — what they did, to whom, when].
Weapons or objects: [what, who had them, where now].
Words used, word for word: “[ ]” — by [whom].
Members of the public present and affected: [number, reaction].
Directions given: [words, to whom, at (time), result].
Cordon or scene: [ ].
sec.why: In a group incident, record each person’s acts separately — joint descriptions don’t survive cross-examination.
cases: Harford v Commissioner of An Garda Síochána

l: The call: [who called, what they said, time]. Who opened the door: [ ]. How I entered: [invited by (who) / power — (Act, section) because (…)].
What I saw and heard: [injuries, damage, disarray, crying, shouting], at [time].
Children present: [names / ages, where they were, what they saw or heard]. Referral: [ ].
sec.why: Record what you saw on arrival before anyone tidies up or changes their account.

l: [Injured party]’s account, taken away from the suspect: “[word for word]” — fear, history: [ ].
[Suspect]’s condition and words: “[word for word]”.
Orders in force (checked on PULSE): [type, terms, served: yes / no].
Risk assessment: [completed — result / by whom].
Support information given: [what, to whom].
sec.why: A withdrawn complaint doesn’t end the duty to protect. Record the risk and what was done about it.

l: Reported by [name, relationship, contact] at [time] on [date], [in person / by phone].
Missing person: [name, date of birth, description, clothing, photo obtained: yes / no].
Last seen: [where, when, by whom, in what condition, with whom].
Risk factors: [age, medical needs and medication, mental health, threats of self-harm, weather, out of character].
Phone: [number, last contact]; social media; bank cards; vehicle [reg].
Places checked: [where, by whom, at what time]; hospitals contacted: [ ].
Risk level: [assessed as (level) by (who) at (time)]. Sergeant told at [time].
sec.why: The first hours matter most. Record the risk factors and every check made, with times.

l: Called by [who] at [time]; arrived at [time]. Present: [who].
The deceased: [name if known], position, clothing, visible injuries, signs of disturbance, medication present.
Death pronounced by [doctor / paramedic — name] at [time].
Scene: [preserved / no suspicious circumstances apparent — why I think so]. Sergeant told at [time].
Identified by: [who, relationship].
Next of kin: [informed by whom, when]; GP: [ ]; coroner’s office: [ ].
Property: [listed, handed to (who) at (time)].
Removed by [undertaker] at [time] to [where].
sec.why: Write down why you concluded there was nothing suspicious — or treat it as a scene.

l: First actions on arrival: [preserving life, safety, resources requested at (time)].
Cordons: [inner and outer, set at (time) by (who)]; scene log started at [time] by [who].
People at the scene: [names or descriptions — and who left, when, which way].
Evidence at risk: [what, how protected, by whom].
Handed over to [rank, name] at [time].
sec.why: The golden hour: what is recorded and protected now decides what can be proved later.
cases: Harford v Commissioner of An Garda Síochána

entries.t: Mental health — s.12 Mental Health Act 2001

l: What I saw and heard that gave me reasonable grounds to believe [the person] was suffering from a mental disorder: [behaviour, their words — “(…)”, information from family or others].
Why, because of that, there was a serious likelihood of immediate and serious harm to [themselves / others]: [what they said or did].
Taken into custody at [time] at [place], told in plain words: “[ ]”. Force: [none / what and why].
Brought to [station / hospital — name] at [time]. Doctor [name] contacted at [time]; examined at [time]; recommendation [made / not made] at [time].
Family or carer contacted: [who, when]. Property and medication: [ ].
sec.why: The belief needs facts behind it. Record what you saw and heard, not a diagnosis. Check the current wording of s.12 before relying on it.

entries.intro: For a draft tailored to the power and your grounds, use the guided Search of the person.

l: Vehicle: [reg, make, colour], [where stopped or found], occupants: [who, which seat].
Power: [s.23 MDA 1977 / s.8 Criminal Law Act 1976 / s.30 OASA 1939 / detained under s.41 RTA 1994 / consent — which] — grounds before the search: [1. …  2. …].
Told the driver and occupants: “[exact words]”. Replies: “[word for word]”.
Searched by [who], areas [boot, glovebox, door pockets, under seats], from [time] to [time]; occupants were [where — watching / not].
Found: [item], exactly where, at [time]; who said what about it: “[ ]”. Exhibit [ref].
Damage caused: [none / what].
sec.why: Say which person you suspect and why — don’t search on autopilot. A lawfully detained vehicle can be opened and what’s found taken.

l: I asked [the person / occupier] whether I could search [what], and told them they did not have to agree and could stop me at any time. My words: “[exact words]”. Their reply: “[word for word]”.
Their capacity to consent: [sober / intoxicated / age / language — how I know they understood].
Written consent: [signed at (time) / not available — why].
What they agreed to: [scope]. Any withdrawal: [at (time), words — search stopped].
Searched by [who], from [time] to [time]. Found: [ ].
sec.why: Consent must be real and informed. Record the words both ways — and if in doubt, use a power instead.

l: Warrant: [Act and section], issued by [judge / Peace Commissioner / Superintendent — name] on [date] at [time], for [premises — check it matches exactly], valid until [ ].
Arrived at [time]; members present: [ ]. Who opened the door: [ ]. Entry: [by consent / by force — how, what damage].
Warrant shown, or copy given, to [occupier] at [time]; words: “[ ]”; reply: “[word for word]”.
People present: [names or descriptions]; searched under [power] if so.
The search: [rooms in order, who searched each, what was found exactly where, who was present when it was found, photographs].
Left at [time]; premises secured [how]; damage noted; receipt for property taken given to [ ].
sec.why: The issuer must have been satisfied on the information, and the warrant must name the right premises. Record the warrant’s details as well as the search.

l: Premises: [dwelling / business / garden / driveway / porch] at [description].
Basis for entering: [invited in by (who) — words: “(…)” / power — (Act, section) because (…) / to save life or prevent serious injury — what I knew].
Any refusal or request to leave: [who, exact words, time] — and what I did then.
Exactly where I went, and when: [driveway / porch / hallway / which rooms].
sec.why: A dwelling is inviolable: an arrest power alone doesn’t let you in. Record permission or refusal word for word, and exactly where you were when.

l: Item: [description, serial numbers, condition, value]; where found: [ ].
Seized under [power] because [reason].
Taken from: [person]; told: “[exact words]”; receipt given: [yes / no].
Packaged in [bag / seal no.], labelled at [time]; stored at [property store — PEMS ref] at [time]; handed to [who] at [time].
sec.why: Keep it safe and keep the chain unbroken. Exhibits lost or disposed of too early have stopped trials.

entries.t: Questions and admissions at the scene

l: Arrested at [time] at [place] under [power].
Arrived at [station] at [time].
Detention authorised by [member in charge — name / number] at [time] under [s.4 CJA 1984 / s.30 OASA 1939 / s.2 CJ(DT)A 1996 / s.50 CJA 2007].
Information on rights given at [time]; solicitor requested at [time], contacted at [time], arrived at [time]; consultation [from–to].
Interviews: [number, from–to, by whom, recorded: yes / no].
Extensions: [rank, name, time, grounds].
Rest, medical or other excluded periods: [from–to, why].
Meals and checks: [times].
Charged / released at [time] by [who]; bail [station / court date].
sec.why: Every minute in custody has to be accounted for. An extension made after the period has run out doesn’t save the detention.
cases: Finnegan v Member in Charge (Santry Garda Station)
People (DPP) v Gormley; People (DPP) v White

l: System: [premises, owner or operator — name, contact]; cameras: [number, positions — which ones are relevant].
Time check: system time [ ] against actual time [ ] — difference [ ].
Viewed by me at [time] on [date]: [what I saw — the times on the footage, the people, what they did].
Copied by [who] to [media] at [time] — exhibit [ref]. Original kept by the owner: [ ].
Request to preserve: [made at (time), to (who), in writing: yes / no]; overwrite period [ ].
sec.why: Ask for CCTV early, and collect what’s offered — failing to retrieve it has quashed convictions. Prove the chain from camera to court.

l: I viewed [footage / stills — which] at [time] on [date], [alone / with (who)]. I [was / was not] told who to look for: [what I was told].
I recognised [the person] as [name].
How I know them: [how often I’ve met them, when last, in what circumstances — for how long, in what light].
What I recognised: [face, gait, build, clothing, voice]. Quality of the footage: [how long they’re visible, angles, clarity].
I made this note at [time], before [being given any further information / seeing PULSE photos].
sec.why: Recognition evidence stands or falls on how well you know the person and how good the footage is — record both, before anything else can colour it.

entries.intro: For an interaction where the person is hostile, or not fully in control of themselves, and a complaint may follow. Write it at the time, factually and in order.

l: On [day] [date] at [time] I was on duty in [uniform / plain clothes] at [exact location], with [members present].
I was there because [call — PULSE incident (ref) / what I saw / I was asked by (who)], for the lawful purpose of [what I was doing].
At [time] I approached [name / description]. I introduced myself: “[exact words — name, station]”, and explained why I was there: “[exact words]”.
Their first response: “[word for word]”.
Their exact words, including abuse, one line each with the time: “[ ]” at [time].
Tone and volume: [ ].
sec.why: Write abuse down exactly as it was said — a summary like “became abusive” proves nothing.

l: What they did: [e.g. stepped to within (distance) of my face, pointed, clenched fists, kicked the door, walked away and came back] at [time].
Avoid labels like “aggressive”, “abusive” or “uncooperative” on their own — say what you saw and heard that led to the word.
sec.why: Labels invite argument; described facts don’t.

l: Signs I saw and heard: [smell of alcohol, slurred speech, unsteady, pupils, confused about time or place, saying things that made no sense — “(word for word)”, distressed, crying].
Age (actual or apparent): [ ]. Language: [understood me — how I know / interpreter needed or offered].
Any vulnerability: [disability or medical condition mentioned, a child present, alone at night].
sec.why: Describe; never diagnose. Your observations are evidence; a medical label from you is opinion.

l: Medical attention offered at [time] — reply: “[ ]”. Ambulance called at [time]: [ ].
Family, carer or friend contacted: [who, when, what they said].
Section 12 of the Mental Health Act considered: [yes — see that entry / no — why not].

sec.h: What I did to calm things
l: How I tried to de-escalate: [lowered my voice, gave them space, explained again, offered options — leaving, calling someone, time to think] at [time]. My words: “[ ]”.
Time I gave them before acting: [ ].
Warning or direction, word for word: “[ ]” at [time], under [power]. Their reply: “[word for word]”.
At [time] they said: “[exact words — e.g. ‘I’m reporting you’]”.
My reply: “[ ]” — [kept to: they are entitled to complain, and how].
Any allegation about me or another member, recorded exactly, without argument: “[ ]”.
sec.why: Record it neutrally. Never argue in your notebook — and never edit the entry once a complaint is made; add a dated note instead.

l: Members present: [names / numbers].
Independent witnesses: [names and contact details — or descriptions], and what they could see from where.
CCTV: [locations]. Body-worn camera: [on at (time) / off — why]; I told them they were being recorded at [time].
Recordings by them or others: [phone, dashcam — who].
Force: [none / what, why, for how long].
Injuries to anyone: [what, where, photographed, first aid given].
Property handled: [returned / seized — receipt].
[They left / were arrested / were handed to (who)] at [time]. Their last words: “[ ]”.
Sergeant [name / number] told at [time]. PULSE [ref]. Body-worn camera footage flagged for retention at [time].
This entry was written at [time] on [date], at [place]. [Made at the time / later because (reason) — my first note was made at (time)].
sec.why: A disputed notebook can decide a case. Make the entry at the time, in order, with nothing added later.

checklist: Write it at the time, or as soon as practicable — and record any delay and why.
Facts, not opinions: what you saw, heard and smelt, and their exact words.
Describe behaviour and state; don’t label or diagnose.
Each member writes their own note, without conferring. If notes were compared, say so and why.
No gaps or blank lines. Cross out with a single line and initial it. Never tear out a page.
Never change an entry after a complaint arrives — add a dated supplementary note instead.
Keep the body-worn camera footage and tell your sergeant.
Write courteously — your notebook may be read aloud in court or at a complaint hearing.
Complaints about Garda conduct now go to Fiosrú, the Office of the Police Ombudsman, which replaced GSOC on 2 April 2025. Check the current process at fiosru.ie.
